name: MCP23017
description: The MCP23017 is a 16-bit general-purpose parallel I/O port expander controlled over a standard I2C interface. The 16 I/O lines are split into two 8-bit ports, PORTA (GPA0-GPA7) and PORTB (GPB0-GPB7), each pin independently configurable as input or output with optional internal weak pull-up and interrupt-on-change. Three hardware address pins (A0-A2) allow up to eight devices on one bus, giving addresses 0x20 to 0x27. Two interrupt outputs, INTA and INTB, can operate per-port or be OR'ed together and configured active-high, active-low, or open-drain. The SPI-interface sibling is the MCP23S17, which shares the same die and package (pins 11/13/14 carry CS/SI/SO instead of the I2C functions).

extra.i2c_address: 0x20 to 0x27, set by A0-A2 (7-bit base 0100 A2 A1 A0)
extra.features: interrupt-on-change, configurable internal weak pull-ups (~100uA), polarity inversion, banked or sequential register modes (IOCON.BANK)
extra.interrupts: INTA/INTB, per-port or OR'ed (MIRROR bit); active-high/low/open-drain

typical_application: Adding 16 extra GPIO (buttons, LEDs, relays) to a microcontroller or single-board computer over a two-wire I2C bus, with up to eight expanders sharing the bus.
gotchas: A0-A2 and RESET must be externally biased; floating them causes erratic behavior. Tie RESET high (to VDD) if you are not driving it.
On the I2C MCP23017, pin 12 is the I2C clock (labeled SCK in the datasheet diagram but functions as SCL) and pins 11 and 14 are NC; on the SPI MCP23S17 those become CS, SI, and SO.
SDA and SCL are open-drain and need external pull-up resistors (the bus provides them); the GPIO weak pull-ups are a separate per-pin feature.
After power-on the IOCON.BANK bit is 0 (sequential register map); libraries written for BANK=1 will read the wrong registers.
The SPDIP, SOIC-28 (wide), and SSOP-28 packages share this exact 1-28 pinout; the QFN package uses a different pin numbering and adds an exposed thermal pad (EP, connect to VSS).
